bg-30-01.hint: Wow, this coffee is really delicious!
bg-30-01.why: -네요 directly expresses real-time pleasant exclamation upon tasting: 맛있- + -네요 = 맛있네요!

bg-30-01.q: Compliment someone's Korean speaking ability with spontaneous exclamation. Use 한국어 + object particle -를 with 정말 잘하시다 + -네요!
bg-30-01.why: -네요 attaches directly to honorific stem 잘하시- to express spontaneous admiration.

steps.en: This food you made yourself is really delicious!

ko: 친구 집에 놀러 갔더니 친구가 직접 만든 피자를 주었어요.
한 입 먹어 보니 치즈도 부드럽고 정말 맛있네요.
친구가 요리를 이렇게 잘하는 줄 몰랐어요.
en: When I visited my friend's house, my friend gave me pizza they made themselves.
Taking a bite, the cheese is soft and wow, it's really delicious.
I didn't know my friend was so good at cooking.

bg-30-01.q: What did the friend give to the writer?
options: Pizza made by the friend
Store-bought cake
A cup of iced tea
bg-30-01.why: The text says '친구가 직접 만든 피자를 주었어요'.

bg-30-01.q: What was the writer's immediate reaction upon taking a bite?
options: The cheese is soft and really delicious
The crust is too salty and dry
The pizza was completely cold
bg-30-01.why: The text states '한 입 먹어 보니 치즈도 부드럽고 정말 맛있네요'.

items: Express spontaneous admiration and surprise upon experiencing sensations with -네요
Compliment friends immediately on looks, skills, and food

items.en: I see / so that's how it is
you must be busy / I see you are busy

bg-30-02.hint: Ah, so that kind of situation existed, I see.
bg-30-02.why: -군요 expresses realization upon learning new information or explanations from others.

bg-30-02.q: Express realization that someone has lived in Korea for a long time. Use 한국에서 오래 with honorific 사시다 + past realization -었군요.
bg-30-02.why: -군요 with honorific past -셨- conveys understanding upon hearing someone's background.

steps.en: Ah, so that was the situation, I didn't know.
Now that I hear your story, I see that was the situation, I didn't know.

ko: 회사 동료가 오늘 피곤해 보여서 무슨 일이 있는지 물어봤어요.
동료가 어젯밤에 늦게까지 프로젝트 보고서를 작성했다고 말했어요.
이야기를 듣고 나니 동료가 왜 피곤한지 이해가 되었고 '정말 고생하셨군요'라고 위로했어요.
en: My coworker looked tired today, so I asked what happened.
My coworker told me they wrote a project report until late last night.
After hearing the story, I understood why they were tired and consoled them: 'You really worked hard!'

bg-30-02.q: Why was the coworker tired today?
options: Because they wrote a report until late last night
Because they went running at 5 AM
Because they watched TV all morning
bg-30-02.why: The text says '동료가 어젯밤에 늦게까지 프로젝트 보고서를 작성했다고 말했어요'.

bg-30-02.q: How did the speaker react upon hearing the reason?
options: Said 'You really worked hard' with understanding
Told them not to drink any coffee
Laughed and asked for snacks

items: React thoughtfully to new information and explanations using -군요
Show empathy and active listening in everyday dialogues

items.en: it is good, isn't it? (seeking agreement)

bg-30-03.hint: The weather is really nice today, isn't it?
bg-30-03.why: -지요 (or spoken -죠) seeks agreement from the listener about an obvious or shared fact.

bg-30-03.q: Confirm the meeting time tomorrow by seeking agreement. Use 내일 회의 with time 2시 + confirmation ending -지요?
bg-30-03.why: Use -지요? to confirm information you believe to be true.

base.en: The weather is nice, isn't it?

steps.en: Today the weather is nice, isn't it?
Today the weather is really warm and nice, isn't it?

ko: 점심시간에 동료들과 함께 회사 근처 공원으로 산책을 나갔어요.
하늘도 푸르고 바람도 솔솔 불어서 '오늘 날씨 정말 좋지요?'라고 물었어요.
동료들도 모두 고개를 끄덕이며 '네, 정말 따뜻하네요'라고 대답했어요.
en: During lunchtime, I went for a walk to the park near the company with coworkers.
The sky was blue and a gentle breeze blew, so I asked: 'The weather is really nice today, isn't it?'
My coworkers all nodded and answered: 'Yes, it's really warm!'

bg-30-03.q: Where did the writer go with coworkers during lunchtime?
options: For a walk to the park near the company
To a department store to shop
To an underground train station
bg-30-03.why: The text says '회사 근처 공원으로 산책을 나갔어요'.

bg-30-03.q: How did the coworkers react when the writer asked about the weather?
options: They nodded and agreed that it was warm
They complained that it was raining
They ran back inside immediately
bg-30-03.why: The text states '동료들도 모두 고개를 끄덕이며 네, 정말 따뜻하네요라고 대답했어요'.

items: Seek agreement or confirm shared facts with -지요? and spoken -죠?
Engage friendly small-talk reactions in daily interactions

bg-30-04.why: -네요 conveys real-time spontaneous praise upon seeing someone's skill: 대단하시네요!

bg-30-04.q: Chime in with spontaneous praise for homemade food. Use 직접 만들다 (ㄹ irregular) + -(으)ㄴ before 음식, and 정말 맛있다 + -네요!
bg-30-04.why: -네요 expresses immediate sensory delight and sincere compliment: 맛있네요!

bg-30-04.wrong: 친구의 설명에 새로 깨달았을 때: 아, 그렇네요!
bg-30-04.hint: When realizing new information from someone's explanation, use 그렇군요 instead of sensory reaction 그렇네요.
bg-30-04.why: Realizing information heard from others uses -군요: 아, 그렇군요!

steps.en: Making it yourself, you are really amazing!
Making this difficult dish yourself, you are really amazing!

ko: 한국 친구와 대화할 때는 적절한 반응으로 맞장구를 치는 것이 좋아요.
맛있는 음식을 함께 먹을 때는 '정말 맛있네요!'라고 감탄하고, 새로운 소식을 들었을 때는 '아, 그렇군요!'라고 공감해요.
그리고 상대방과 이미 아는 생각을 나눌 때는 '맞지요?'라고 확인하면 대화가 한층 부드러워져요.
en: When conversing with a Korean friend, chiming in with suitable reactions is great.
When eating delicious food together, exclaim 'It's really delicious! (-네요)', and when hearing new news, empathize with 'Ah, I see! (-군요)'.
And when sharing known thoughts with the other person, confirming with 'That's right, isn't it? (-지요)' makes the conversation much smoother.

bg-30-04.q: What should you say when tasting delicious food together to exclaim with delight?
options: '정말 맛있네요!' (It's really delicious!)
'정말 맛없을 거예요' (It will not be delicious)
'정말 먹지 마십시오' (Please do not eat)
bg-30-04.why: The text says '맛있는 음식을 함께 먹을 때는 정말 맛있네요!라고 감탄하고'.

bg-30-04.q: What is the effect of using appropriate reaction words in Korean conversation?
options: The conversation becomes much smoother and warmer
The other person stops talking
The conversation quickly becomes an argument
bg-30-04.why: The text concludes '대화가 한층 부드러워져요' (the conversation becomes much smoother).

items: Skillfully alternate between -네요, -군요, and -지요 in lively Korean conversations
Be an engaging and responsive conversation partner using natural 맞장구 expressions
